title: 5 ancient Windows relics still running inside Windows 11
summary: Even with a new face, Windows 11 still leans on the 90s.
content: Windows 11 looks modern, with rounded corners, a centered Start menu, and icons that look nothing like the 90s. Underneath, a surprising number of ancient features are still present and actually doing real work.

title: 6 book-to-movie crossovers that died after the first film
summary: Several of these books are about to adapted for the screen again, because one failure wasn't enough.
content: 2001 was an important year for movie franchises. In November, Warner Bros. Pictures released Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone , based on the book by J.K. Rowling. It set off an eight-movie franchise that is still paying dividends today. Just a month later, New Line Cinema released The Fellowship of the Ring , the first movie in the tremendously popular Lord of the Rings franchise, based on the books by J.R.R. Tolkien.
tags: The Mortal Instruments: City of Bones

title: I fall asleep watching videos, so I made Android stop playing when I do
summary: I've been giving YouTubers watch time in my sleep for far too long.
content: I’ve lost count of how many nights I’ve put on a YouTube video in bed, closed my eyes for just a second, and woken up with zero clue what I just watched. Autoplay will happily entertain an audience of absolutely nobody while I'm knocked out cold, leaving my phone dangerously low on battery by morning.

title: Audio-Technica’s strangest headphones don’t cover my ears, and now my earbuds feel claustrophobic
summary: These ear-fit headphones might replace your wired earbuds.
content: I've tried many different pairs of headphones and earbuds, but the Audio-Technica ATH-EQ300M headphones proved to be unlike any other. They're technically stereo headphones, although you wouldn't guess that by looking at them. These are what Audio-Technica calls "ear-fit headphones," and they lack a traditional headband. Instead, they clip onto your ear with plastic pieces, using 28mm drivers to fill your ears with sound while allowing you to maintain awareness of your surroundings.

title: You’re probably ignoring your Pixel’s most useful feature (I did too)
summary: It's hiding in plain sight.
content: Pixel phones may look pretty simple, but they come packed with features that are easy to miss . For instance, its app drawer search bar looks like the one on any other Android phone, but it’s actually way more capable than simply opening apps. It can dig into your contacts, run web searches, find an app on the Play Store, find a setting buried several menus deep, and do a lot more.

title: Chrome has a setting that cuts its memory use by up to 10%
summary: Memory Saver freed 520 MB across 30 tabs in testing and costs nothing to enable.
content: Tab hoarding is a problem everywhere , but it's an even bigger problem on Google Chrome where undisciplined tab management can make your system slow. Chrome is notorious for high memory usage and consistently ranks among the most memory-intensive browsers in most tests . However, if you know where to look, Chrome offers a way to reduce memory usage by managing tabs efficiently and it genuinely works.

title: DRM on Linux is a nightmare no one seems to address
summary: Denuvo and the mystery PC activation limit.
content: If there’s one thing that really grinds my gears, it’s game DRM. Some might call it a necessity, a byproduct of the war against piracy. Which would be all well and good, if the anti-tamper worked as intended. The more modern iterations of game DRM (read: Denuvo) have been a massive pain to deal with, especially on Linux, where you’ll all too often keep running into the dreaded activation lockout.

title: An Ethernet cable was all I needed to connect two Windows 11 PCs
summary: A local, high-speed link between machines.
content: There are seemingly endless ways to transfer a file between computers , from cables and storage drives to cloud storage services and even messaging apps. I have to admit, I use Slack to move photos and files across devices more than any other method. It's quick, free, and it just works. Some people swear by using their email or Discord account for file sharing, but the simplest and fastest method of transferring a file between computers might just be Ethernet.

title: Gmail is dropping three features in 2027, and that means it's time to rethink my email setup
summary: Google giveth, Google taketh away.
content: Email addresses really pile up over the years. You've probably got a personal one, a work one, and maybe even an old Hotmail account that's somehow still tied to a bunch of important logins. Juggling all of them is way easier when Gmail lets you handle everything from a single browser tab.

title: My GPU memory was maxed out, and this free tool told me exactly why
summary: Every megabyte of VRAM accounted for, including the spill into system RAM.
content: Windows Task Manager can tell you how much of your GPU memory is in use, but it can't tell you what's filling it. Knowing the why is important when you're running local AI models on your PC and your GPU memory spills into system RAM, slowing everything down with no clear explanation.

title: GTA 6's 30 FPS lock didn’t last a week on jailbroken PS5s
summary: An unofficial patch for GTA 6 pushes the game's framerate to as high as 60FPS on PS5 consoles.
content: Modders have already managed to run GTA 6 on jailbroken PS5 consoles without requiring the newest firmware by backporting a fix for the hypervisor exploit. This jailbreak version comes with another surprise: an FPS unlocker that pushes the game on PS5 consoles to as high as 60FPS.

title: How to get perfect PDF exports from Microsoft Excel every time
summary: Your spreadsheet shouldn't fall apart just because you saved it as a PDF.
content: You’d think exporting your Excel spreadsheet to PDF would be a no-brainer. After all, you've already done the hard work of organizing your data, creating tables, and getting your formatting right. Yet when you open the exported PDF, you might find columns awkwardly split across multiple pages, portions of text missing, borders thicker than they should be, or even blank pages appearing out of nowhere.

title: Kodi can play your Plex and Jellyfin libraries, and it's the best app for both
summary: Use Kodi to customize and manage your existing Plex and Jellyfin configurations for a much better overall user experience.
content: I’ve long been a fan of Plex and Jellyfin for organizing and streaming my personal media, but I've always preferred Kodi’s customization flexibility and extensive add-on library. Thankfully, Kodi lets you connect Plex and Jellyfin, so you can browse and play your existing libraries without abandoning your favorite media server.

title: I removed my Lenovo Legion Go’s controllers and turned it into a pocket computer
summary: A full Windows PC in my pocket.
content: Most people pick between a compact 13- or 14-inch laptop or a larger 15- or 16-inch laptop and swear by their size choice, but I don't fall into either camp. I prefer laptops that are absurdly thin, light, and compact. The flawed 12-inch Retina MacBook comes closest to successfully executing my dream laptop form factor, but it's borderline unusable in 2026. Foldable phones and tablets fall short as portable workstations, and although I'm primarily a macOS user, Apple doesn't make a MacBook small enough.

title: Microsoft is replacing Windows PowerShell after years of neglect
summary: It's time to sweep 5.1 aside for PowerShell 7.
content: PowerShell 5.1 is gone. It's done. Well, almost. In mid-November 2026, Microsoft announced PowerShell 5.1 is "no longer in active development," meaning that, over time, its feature set will dwindle compared to newer versions, basically making it more difficult to use.

title: My Android's camera cutout is now the most useful part of my screen
summary: Use that notch
content: Smartphones moved from thick bezels to pop-up cameras , flip cameras, and finally settled on the notch. While that notch doesn't take up much screen real estate, it still takes space, and it does nothing except house the selfie camera. Thankfully, there are a bunch of apps that make your phone’s camera cutout useful .

title: 8 Apple-made apps that don't come preinstalled on your iPhone
summary: Apple made them for a reason—check them out.
content: Unsurprisingly, your iPhone comes with several Apple-made apps such as Weather, Health, Files, and Notes. However, that’s just the start. Apple also offers a range of other useful apps that are definitely worth checking out.

title: These 5 self-hosted apps keep working when your internet doesn’t
summary: The internet goes down. Your lights, movies, and paperwork shouldn't.
content: An internet outage has a funny way of revealing just how little of your digital life actually lives offline now. Your files are somewhere else, your entertainment needs permission to play, and even switching on the light means a return trip to some distant server.

title: 7 smart TV privacy settings I should have checked right after buying
summary: Turns out it was spying on me all the time.
content: When I bought my LG OLED, I did what most folks probably do: I breezed through the user agreements with my remote, doing everything necessary to make them disappear. From there, I went straight to the antenna channel scan. I didn't think about that setup until earlier this year when Gamers Nexus, Level1Techs, and outside security researchers released a damning privacy report on YouTube on LG's webOS TVs.

title: Your smart TV, smart plugs, and NAS are the weakest links in your home network
summary: 67% of home network flaws come from three devices you never think about.
content: You've probably spent a good amount of time and effort picking out a router and setting a decent Wi-Fi password. Meanwhile, the TV in your living room, those cheap smart plugs you've got around the house, and your NAS sitting quietly in the corner are doing the opposite of securing your network.

title: Every GTA radio station is now streaming free in your browser
summary: From DJ Cara’s Non-Stop Pop FM in GTA V to the OG Flash FM in Vice City, this website lets you stream the entire GTA radio collection.
content: Made by a developer named Shrikar, GTAMusic.fun lets you stream every radio station from every GTA game. From the original Grand Theft Auto to the latest installment in the series, the site brings together decades of some of the most nostalgic songs in video games.

title: Windows laptops still answer strangers on public Wi-Fi because of a protocol from 2007
summary: Your laptop may ask a whole coffee shop for directions.
content: Connecting to public Wi-Fi and getting on with your day is a normal part of life, but if Windows tries to reach a network resource it cannot find, your computer can end up asking almost everyone on that public Wi-Fi for directions.

title: Your DDR5 RAM is running slower than what the box says
summary: Your DDR5 RAM is probably slower than it should be, and it's an easy fix.
content: DDR5 memory runs at breakneck speeds, about 1.5–2x higher data rates than DDR4 in general, starting from 4,800MT/s to even 8,000MT/s+ in some cases.
